[project]
name = "mcp-hangar"
version = "2.31.0"
description = "Policy enforcement plane for MCP: every tool call ends in a verdict. Self-hosted, MIT."
readme = "README.md"
license = {text = "MIT"}
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [
    {name = "Marcin Pyrka", email = "marcin@mcp-hangar.io"}
]
keywords = ["mcp", "model-context-protocol", "llm", "ai", "security", "policy-enforcement", "tool-poisoning"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries",
    "Topic :: System :: Systems Administration",
]
dependencies = [
    # Pinned EXACTLY, not merely bounded. This pin is a contract with the SDK, and
    # what it protects against is a wrong wire, not an ImportError.
    #
    # Why exact: `_sdk_compat` shims SDK internals (`_lowlevel_server`,
    # `add_request_handler`, `MCPError`, `HANDSHAKE_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS`), the front
    # door installs its own `tools/list` and `tools/call` handlers, and the relay
    # registers `tasks/*` methods the SDK deliberately does not carry in
    # `SPEC_CLIENT_METHODS`. Any of those can change between two SDK releases
    # without a failing import, and 2.3.0 proved it: it stopped running the
    # `tools/list` handler before dispatch and asked `get_tool_input_schema`
    # instead, so every `Mcp-Param-*` check on a projected tool was silently
    # skipped (#1791) -- a deny that did not deny.
    #
    # How to move it: run the weekly canary against the candidate (#1793), then
    # the full integration tier, the relay smoke (`task-relay-smoke.yml`, by
    # dispatch) and the conformance workflow. A failure there is the pin doing its
    # job. Move `mcp` and `mcp-types` together to the same version, and raise the
    # floors in `scripts/check_dependency_floors.py` that the move implies.
    #
    # The v1 line on `main` solves the same class of problem with `>=1.28.1,<2`
    # (#561): both branches must be unable to follow the SDK somewhere their
    # code does not run. Do not widen either to match the other.
    "mcp==2.3.0",
    "mcp-types==2.3.0",  # v2 split protocol-types dist (imported directly as mcp_types); paired with mcp
    "structlog>=24.0.0",
    # Mirrors the floor `mcp==2.3.0` declares; we inherit it rather than choose it.
    # Declared at the same value so the metadata cannot claim an install that the
    # resolver can never produce (see scripts/check_dependency_floors.py).
    "pydantic>=2.12.0",
    # Capped below 1.0: httpx 1.0 drops `httpx.AsyncClient`, which this code
    # uses everywhere. Unbounded, `pip install --pre mcp-hangar` -- the install
    # the v2-preview docs recommend -- resolves httpx to 1.0.dev3 and the
    # gateway dies at startup. Same class as the `mcp` cap (#561): a dependency
    # allowed to walk into a major this code does not run on.
    "httpx>=0.25.0,<1",
    "prometheus-client>=0.19.0",
    # Security floors: pip leaves an already-installed version alone while it
    # satisfies the constraint, so a floor is what an existing environment keeps.
    # pyjwt 2.13.0 fixes CVE-2026-48522/48523/48524/48525/48526 and CVE-2026-32597;
    # 48524 and 48525 are pre-auth DoS on the JWKS path (`get_signing_key_from_jwt`).
    # 2.14.0 fixes PYSEC-2026-4140 and 4142..4152 (4145: an HMAC/asymmetric
    # allow-list accepts a non-canonical PEM public key as the HMAC secret);
    # 2.15.0 fixes PYSEC-2026-4141.
    # `[crypto]` because JWKS RS256/ES256 needs it; it arrived only via `mcp` before.
    "pyjwt[crypto]>=2.15.0",
    # 50.0.0 fixes CVE-2026-69247; 49.0.0 fixes CVE-2026-69248/69249.
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
    # not imported directly; arrives via mcp/httpx/starlette. 4.14.2 fixes
    # GHSA-82r6-8w77-94w6 (TLSStream IDNA 2003 host name encoding) and
    # GHSA-5p39-cfhj-2xmp (process-pool workers blocked on undrained stderr).
    "anyio>=4.14.2",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "docker>=7.1.0",
    "aiosqlite>=0.19.0",
    "typer>=0.12.0",
    "rich>=13.0.0",
    "questionary>=2.0.0",
    # not imported directly; declared to raise the floor inherited via mcp/starlette
    # (mcp alone asks for >=0.0.9). 0.0.31 fixes CVE-2026-53537..53540.
    "python-multipart>=0.0.31",
    "protobuf>=6.33.5",
    "jcs>=0.2.1",
    "click>=8.3.3",  # security floor: PYSEC-2026-2132 (click.edit() command injection); transitive via typer
    # not imported directly; uvicorn needs a WebSocket library to upgrade a
    # connection, and without one `/api/ws/events` answers 404 (#1676). Only the
    # Dockerfile installed it before. 16.0 is the first release with Python 3.14
    # wheels, above uvicorn[standard]'s own >=13.0 and every known advisory (<9.1).
    "websockets>=16.0",
]
[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=9.0.3",  # security floor: CVE-2025-71176 (tmpdir handling)
    "pytest-cov>=4.1.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.3.0",  # first release that admits pytest 9 (the pytest floor above)
    "pytest-timeout>=2.2.0",
    "pytest-benchmark>=5.1.0",
    # Parallel runs: CI passes `-n auto --dist loadfile` (see ci-core.yml).
    "pytest-xdist>=3.6.0",
    # Pinned, not a floor: this is the version CI lints with. A floor would let
    # every machine resolve a different ruff, which is how a rule that fires
    # locally stays invisible in CI. Dependabot bumps it (uv ecosystem), and CI
    # follows automatically because it installs from here.
    "ruff==0.17.0",
    "import-linter==2.15",
    "mypy>=1.8.0",
    "hypothesis>=6.90.0",
    "jsonschema>=4.20.0",
    # The discovery security check's HTTP client (security_validator.py). In a
    # deployment the kubernetes extra brings it; without it here the check is
    # skipped in every test run and its tests can only skip (#1756). Security
    # floor: the deps-floor-audit job refuses anything older than 3.14.4.
    "aiohttp>=3.14.4",
]
# The kubernetes discovery source imports this. Until now it was declared
# nowhere -- not a dependency, not an extra, not in the image -- so the source
# could not be constructed on any supported install: bootstrap took the
# ImportError path, logged `discovery_source_unavailable` and discovered
# nothing, while the guide, the cookbook and the config reference all described
# a working feature. `docker` is a base dependency, so its source always worked;
# this is the same standing for kubernetes.
# The fuzzing harnesses under `fuzz/`. Markered, not bare: atheris publishes
# manylinux x86_64 wheels for CPython 3.12-3.14 ONLY, so an unconditional entry
# would break `uv sync --all-extras` on this project's own 3.11 baseline and on
# every macOS machine. The invariants the harnesses assert live in
# `fuzz/invariants.py`, which imports nothing from atheris and is replayed by
# the normal test suite everywhere.
fuzz = ["atheris>=3.1.0; sys_platform == 'linux' and python_version >= '3.12' and platform_machine == 'x86_64'"]
kubernetes = ["kubernetes>=29.0.0"]
# 1.35 is the lowest release that installs beside the core dependencies:
# `opentelemetry-proto` requires `protobuf<6` through 1.34.x, and the core
# requires `protobuf>=6.33.5` (`mcp` alone already needs the API at >=1.28).
opentelemetry = [
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.35.0",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.35.0",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp>=1.35.0",
]
# The PostgreSQL stores import psycopg2 -- see `database_common.PostgresConnectionFactory`.
# This extra declared `asyncpg`, which appears nowhere in `src/` outside a docstring,
# so `pip install mcp-hangar[postgres]` installed a library nothing imports and left
# the driver unable to start (#779). Same failure shape as the kubernetes extra (#770),
# harder to notice because the extra existed and was merely wrong.
postgres = [
    "psycopg2-binary>=2.9.9",
]
# The truncation continuation cache's redis driver imports this (#1008). Same
# class as [postgres]: cluster-only, off the base install AND off `full` so a
# laptop stays small; the published image installs it (see Dockerfile).
redis = [
    "redis>=5.0.0",
]
full = [
    "fpdf2>=2.8.0",
]
[project.scripts]
mcp-hangar = "mcp_hangar.server.cli:cli_main"
[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://mcp-hangar.io"
Documentation = "https://mcp-hangar.io/docs/getting-started/quickstart"
Repository = "https://github.com/mcp-hangar/mcp-hangar"
[build-system]
# hatchling is PINNED. 1.32.1 (published 2026-09-16) loads a builder plugin
# chain whose binary builder imports the `hatch` CLI package
# (`hatchling/builders/binary.py`: `from hatch.plugin.manager import
# PluginManager`). That package is NOT present in the isolated build env that
# `hatch build` and `python -m build` each create from this `requires` list, so
# every build path died with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hatch'` --
# the Docker image, the `build` CI job, `make build-core` and the release
# workflow. 1.32.0 is unaffected. See #1513.
#
# This one pin covers every path because all of them resolve the backend from
# this list. Before lifting it, check that a newer hatchling no longer imports
# `hatch` at plugin-load time, then prove it with `docker build .` and the
# `build` job -- not with a local `pip install`, which has `hatch` on hand and
# therefore cannot reproduce the failure.
requires = ["hatchling==1.32.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"
[tool.hatch.build]
exclude = ["/.github/brand"]
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Cyclomatic complexity ceiling for NEW code. Everything above it today carries an
# explicit `# noqa: C901` naming its current score -- 16 functions, listed by
# `ruff check src --select C901`. That list is a debt ledger, not wallpaper: it is
# short enough to read, and each entry is visible to whoever next opens the
# function.
#
# 15 rather than mccabe's default 10 because 10 would have baselined 54 functions,
# and a 54-entry noqa list stops being read. Anything above 15 is indefensible in
# review, so the gate bites real monsters while leaving ordinary code alone.
#
# The rule: never add a noqa here. Lower the ceiling, or split the function.
max-complexity = 15

# Mypy strictness migration in progress (TASK-P1-5).
# Phase 1: baseline strictness with per-module debt overrides (DONE).
# Phase 2: clean union-attr + attr-defined site by site.
# Phase 3: enable disallow_untyped_defs, drop all per-module overrides.
# Goal: zero overrides + strict = true by 2026-Q4.
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
strict = false
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = false      # TODO(mypy-phase-3): enable
disallow_incomplete_defs = false   # TODO(mypy-phase-3): enable
check_untyped_defs = true
no_implicit_optional = true
show_error_codes = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
# disable_error_code intentionally absent -- per-module overrides below
# carry the technical debt explicitly. Goal: zero per-module overrides
# by 2026-Q4 (tracked in the issue tracker; see TODO(mypy-phase-3) above).
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "docker.*",
    "yaml.*",
    "prometheus_client.*",

    "psycopg2.*",

[tool.coverage.run]
# branch = true lives HERE, not only on the command line, for two reasons.
# 1. The decision-path floors are BRANCH numbers. A floor compared against
#    statement-only data silently passes a lower bar than it claims.
# 2. Modes do not mix: combining a statement-mode .coverage with a branch-mode
#    run raises `coverage.exceptions.DataError: Can't combine branch coverage
#    data with statement data` as a pytest INTERNALERROR. Making every run
#    branch-mode removes the mixed state entirely.
branch = true
relative_files = true

[tool.coverage.report]
# Deliberately NO fail_under. coverage.py's threshold is GLOBAL -- there is no
# per-file setting -- so a single number would have to be low enough for the
# weakest module in the tree, which is exactly the modules that need the
# strongest guarantee. Per-module floors live below and are checked by
# scripts/check_decision_coverage.py.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision-path coverage floors
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A module is a DECISION PATH when a wrong branch produces a wrong allow/deny:
# authorization, human consent, egress and tool-access policy, supply-chain
# digest pinning. An untested branch there is a security defect, not a style
# complaint, so these modules get a floor and the rest of the tree does not.
#
# Values are combined line+branch coverage as MEASURED on this branch, rounded
# down -- not an aspirational 90. A gate that is red the day it lands teaches
# people to skip it; this one is green on arrival and catches regressions from
# the first commit. Raising a floor is the unit of progress
# (`check_decision_coverage.py coverage.json --bump` locks in what was gained).
#
# Floors are measured on the Python the GATE runs (3.11 in the decision-coverage
# job), not on a developer's interpreter. Branch-arc counts differ between CPython
# versions: server/tools/batch/executor.py measures 85.38 on 3.13 and 85.06 on
# 3.11, so a floor taken from 3.13 failed CI on arrival. When a floor moves, take
# the number from the CI job -- or the lower of the two if you have both.
#
#   server/tools/batch/executor.py at 84.5 -- deliberately below what anyone
#     measures locally. The module runs work on a thread pool with timeouts and
#     single-flight de-duplication, so a handful of branches fire or not
#     depending on scheduling. Measured: 85.38 three times on CPython 3.13,
#     85.06 twice on 3.11, and 85.06 then 84.75 on two CI runs of the same
#     tree. Local is reproducible; a loaded shared runner is not. The floor sits
#     under the lowest observed CI value rather than under the local one, so the
#     gate reports a real regression instead of the runner's mood.
#     Pinning those branches with deterministic tests would let this rise again.
#
# Two entries are visible debt rather than a target:
#   approvals/persistence/sqlite_approval_repository.py at 87.0 -- the store
#     holding approval state, tenant scoping and the arguments hash. Unit tests
#     use a fake repository; the real SQL of `transition` is exercised by the
#     multi-process race test (#1794) and the CLI resolve tests (#1778).
#   domain/value_objects/tool_access_policy.py at 84.2 -- _CompositePolicy's
#     merge and approval-list handling, i.e. the consent-preservation logic.
#   server/tools/batch/executor.py at 85.3 -- the invoke path, including the
#     455-line _execute_call_inner.
[tool.decision_coverage]
# How far a floor may sit below reality before it stops being a ratchet.
drift_allowance = 3.0

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# No `addopts`. It used to carry `-v --cov=mcp_hangar --cov-report=term-missing`,
# which put an 18-second coverage pass and 6600 lines of per-test output on every
# local run, including runs of a single file. The jobs that read a coverage report
# ask for it explicitly, and the live tiers had to undo it with `-o addopts=""`
# because coverage of a subprocess under test measures nothing.
# Per-test hang guard: fail (with a stack dump) instead of hanging so one wedged
# test can't burn a CI job to the 6h ceiling (which cancelled a release). 300s is
# far above any real test; the whole unit suite runs in well under a minute.
timeout = 300
pythonpath = ["src", "."]
markers = [
    "benchmark: performance benchmarks (deselect with '-m not benchmark')",
    "security: security-related tests",
    "live: black-box live verification against a running hangar (opt-in; skips without prerequisites)",
    "t0: live tier 0 -- single process + stub backend",
    "t1: live tier 1 -- multi-backend / groups (needs compose)",
    "t2: live tier 2 -- auth / IdP (needs Keycloak)",
]
[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "mypy>=1.19.1",
    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
    "vulture>=2.14",
]

# Events a handler listens for that nothing emits, with the reason. Kept here
# rather than as string literals in the test: the dead-symbol scanner counts a
# name appearing in Python source as a reference, so an inventory of dead
# vocabulary written in code would hide exactly the symbols it inventories.

  "DetectionRuleMatched:anomaly detection is deliberately unshipped; the enforcement handler is built and waiting",
  "BehavioralDeviationDetected:same feature -- risk scoring consumes it, nothing produces it yet",
  "EgressBlocked:the metrics handler counts it; L7 egress enforcement emits the observed variant instead",
  "TaskInputRequired:the synchronous mid-flight consent flow that emitted it was removed with SEP-2663",
]
# Events with neither a producer nor a consumer. May shrink, never grow.
unused_events = [
  "DiscoveryCycleCompleted", "DiscoverySourceHealthChanged",
  "McpServerApproved", "McpServerCapabilityQuarantineReleased", ]

# FR-951: preview is enabled solely to reach PLW1514; explicit-preview-rules

    "E",      # pycodestyle errors

]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Vulture whitelist uses bare expressions and grouped imports by design
"vulture_whitelist.py" = ["B018", "E402"]
# C901 gate scoped to yamlgraph/ per FR-221; examples/projects/scripts excluded
"examples/**/*.py" = ["C901"]
"projects/**/*.py" = ["C901"]
"scripts/**/*.py" = ["C901"]
# Tests use assert statements and subprocess calls by design
"tests/**" = ["S101", "S602", "S603", "S607", "S108"]
"scripts/vscode/tests/**" = ["S101"]
"scripts/tests/**" = ["S101"]
".github/hooks/tests/**" = ["S101", "S603"]
# Examples demonstrate patterns; subprocess/binding/assert-in-tests are intentional
"examples/**" = ["S101", "S603", "S607", "S104", "S105", "S108", "S112"]
# Scripts use partial executable paths (git, etc.) by design
"scripts/**" = ["S603", "S607"]

addopts = "--cov=yamlgraph --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=85"

    "slow: marks tests that take >1 second to complete",

[tool.coverage.run]

[tool.coverage.report]

]

# Python project configuration for DeepTutor
# This file configures Black, Ruff, and other Python tools

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=61.0", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "deeptutor"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "An agent-native intelligent learning companion with multi-agent collaboration and RAG"
# Python 3.14 is supported by the core app now that compiled base dependencies
# such as FAISS publish compatible wheels. Keep a forward cap so a future
# interpreter is not advertised before the compiled dependency stack is ready.
# Individual optional integrations may carry tighter markers below.
requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.15"
readme = "README.md"
license = {text = "Apache-2.0"}
dependencies = [
    # Core runtime
    "PyYAML>=6.0",
    "jinja2>=3.1.0",
    "openai>=1.30.0",
    "tiktoken>=0.5.0",
    "aiohttp>=3.9.4",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
    "requests>=2.32.2",
    "ddgs>=9.9.1",
    "nest_asyncio>=1.5.8",
    "tenacity>=8.0.0",
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.0.0",
    "packaging>=24.2",
    "jsonschema>=4.20.0,<5.0.0",
    "aiosqlite>=0.19.0",
    "typer>=0.9.0",
    "rich>=13.0.0",
    "prompt_toolkit>=3.0.36",
    "pyte>=0.8.1",  # in-memory terminal emulator: scrape Claude Code's /model TUI on sync
    # MCP client. Core rather than a `partners`-only extra (issue #792): the
    # default chat/tool surface includes configurable MCP servers, so a plain
    # install must be able to connect them without an optional extra.
    "mcp>=1.26.0,<2.0.0",
    "pageindex>=0.2.10,<0.3.0",
    # Partner channel QR onboarding (WeChat, WeCom, Feishu). Same reasoning as
    # `mcp` above: scan-based onboarding is part of the default partner setup
    # surface, it is pure Python with no compiled or system dependencies, and
    # without it the browser renders no code at all — the operator sees a
    # button that does nothing, with no error to explain why.
    "qrcode>=7.4.0,<9.0.0",
    # IANA time zone database for `zoneinfo`. Windows ships none, so without
    # it every named zone (even "UTC") is unknown there and usage statistics,
    # practice reviews and cron schedules reject every timezone they are given.
    # On Linux/macOS `zoneinfo` keeps preferring the system database.
    "tzdata>=2024.1",
    # Full app dependencies included by default for `pip install deeptutor`.
    "anthropic>=0.30.0",
    "dashscope>=1.14.0",
    "perplexityai>=0.1.0",
    "oauth-cli-kit>=0.1.1",
    "llama-index>=0.14.12",
    # The current BM25 integration pins PyStemmer <3, whose 2.x line has no
    # Python 3.14 wheels. Skip it there so ordinary installs never require a C
    # compiler; the retriever already falls back to vector search when absent.
    "bm25s>=0.3.14,<0.4.0",  # Legacy page lookup without optional PyStemmer
    "llama-index-retrievers-bm25>=0.7.1,<0.8.0; python_version < '3.14'",
    # FAISS vector store: vectorized ANN retrieval that replaces SimpleVectorStore's
    # brute-force per-query scan for large knowledge bases (issue #552). The
    # pipeline imports it lazily and falls back to SimpleVectorStore if absent.
    "llama-index-vector-stores-faiss>=0.4.0,<1.0.0",
    "faiss-cpu>=1.8.0,<2.0.0; python_version < '3.14'",
    "faiss-cpu>=1.12.0,<2.0.0; python_version >= '3.14'",

    "defusedxml>=0.7.1",

    "python-multipart>=0.0.6",

# ============================================

# Target Python version

line-length = 100

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Enable only foundational lint rules (intentionally relaxed)
select = [
    "E",   # pycodestyle errors (语法错误)

    "I",   # isort (import 排序)

]

extend-select = [
    "B006",  # Do not use mutable data structures for argument defaults

# Ignore specific rules (keep the lint profile relaxed)

    "E501",  # Line too long (handled by formatter)
    "B008",  # Do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    "PLR0911", # Too many return statements
    "PLR0912", # Too many branches
    "PLR0913", # Too many arguments
    "PLR0915", # Too many statements
    "PLR2004", # Magic value used in comparison
    "TRY003", # Avoid specifying long messages outside exception class
    "T201",  # print found (allowed for debugging scripts)
    "E722",  # Do not use bare except (kept relaxed for legacy paths)
    "E402",  # Module level import not at top of file (kept relaxed)
    "PLC0415", # import should be at top-level (kept relaxed)
    "PTH123", # open() should be replaced by Path.open() (standard open allowed)
    "PTH103", # os.makedirs() should be replaced by Path.mkdir() (os.makedirs allowed)
    "PTH118", # os.path.join() should be replaced by Path (os.path.join allowed)
    "EM101",  # Exception must not use a string literal
    "EM102",  # Exception must not use an f-string literal
    "TRY002", # Create your own exception
    "TRY300", # Consider moving this statement to an else block
    "DTZ005", # datetime.now() called without tz argument
    "RET504", # Unnecessary assignment before return
    "PLW2901", # for loop variable overwritten by assignment target
    "F841",  # Local variable assigned but never used
    "ERA001", # Found commented-out code (kept relaxed)
]

# Exclude patterns

    ".bzr",
    ".direnv",
    ".eggs",
    ".git",
    ".git-rewrite",
    ".hg",
    ".mypy_cache",
    ".nox",
    ".pants.d",
    ".pyenv",
    ".pytest_cache",
    ".pytype",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".svn",
    ".tox",
    ".venv",

    "build",
    "dist",
    "node_modules",
    ".next",
    "out",
    "venv",

[tool.ruff.format]

quote-style = "double"
# Indent with spaces

# Automatically detect the appropriate line ending

# ============================================

# B101=assert, B311=random, B403/B404=pickle/subprocess imports

[project]
name = "soctalk"
version = "0.2.1"
description = "SecOps LLM Agent using LangGraph with Wazuh, Cortex, and TheHive integration via MCP"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"
license = {text = "Apache-2.0"}
authors = [
    {name = "Gianluca Brigandi"}
]
keywords = ["secops", "siem", "langgraph", "mcp", "security", "incident-response"]

dependencies = [
    "langgraph>=0.2.0",
    "langchain>=0.3.0",
    "langchain-anthropic>=0.3.0",
    "langchain-openai>=0.3.0",
    "mcp>=1.0.0,<2",  # cap: the image installs unpinned (pip install .); 2.x renamed Tool.inputSchema and broke worker enrichment (#111). Lift once 2.x is validated.
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0.0",
    "aiohttp>=3.9.0",
    "rich>=13.0.0",
    "structlog>=24.0.0",
    "sqlmodel>=0.0.22",
    "asyncpg>=0.29.0",
    "greenlet>=3.0.0",
    "alembic>=1.13.0",
    "fastapi>=0.115.0",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.32.0",
    "sse-starlette>=2.1.0",
    "psycopg2-binary>=2.9.0",
    # V1 additions (codex P1-7):
    "prometheus-client>=0.20.0",
    "kubernetes>=29.0.0",
    # Async client for cross-namespace Secret reads from the chat agent
    # (per-tenant Wazuh routing). The sync ``kubernetes`` package would
    # block the event loop.
    "kubernetes-asyncio>=32.0.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    # Internal auth (internal-auth):
    "argon2-cffi>=23.1.0",
    # First-party IANA tz database so zoneinfo.ZoneInfo resolves legacy
    # backward-compat aliases (e.g. America/Buenos_Aires) in slim container
    # images whose system tzdata omits the `backward` links. Without it the
    # flight-recorder fleet-day endpoint 400s "unknown timezone" for browsers
    # that report a legacy zone, blanking the whole panel. See fleet_day.py.
    "tzdata>=2024.1",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.0.0",
    "ruff>=0.1.0",
    "mypy>=1.8.0",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",         # TestClient dep for FastAPI unit tests
]

[project.scripts]
soctalk-auth = "soctalk.core.cli.auth:main"
soctalk-prices = "soctalk.core.cli.prices:main"
soctalk-backfill-prices = "soctalk.core.cli.backfill_prices:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/soctalk", "src/soctalk_wire", "src/soctalk_entities"]
# The price catalog seed ships with the package: v1_0042 creates the table but
# deliberately seeds no rows, so a fresh install has no rates until an operator
# runs `soctalk-prices import`. Without the file in the wheel there is nothing
# to import, and every model resolves `unknown` -> the fail-expensive fallback.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"data/pricing" = "soctalk/data/pricing"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "N", "W", "UP"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# The demo-seed corpus is authored prose (verdict/threat text): long
# string literals can't be mechanically wrapped without harming the copy.
"scripts/demo-seed/*.py" = ["E501"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
strict = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
testpaths = ["tests"]
markers = [
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests requiring PostgreSQL (deselect with '-m \"not integration\"')",
]
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"

    "pyspark>=4.0.1",
]

[project.scripts]
benchbox = "benchbox.cli.app:main"
benchbox-mcp = "benchbox.mcp.cli:main"

[project.urls]
"Homepage" = "https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox"
"Bug Tracker" = "https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/issues"
"Documentation" = "https://benchbox.dev/docs/"
"Repository" = "https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox.git"
"Changelog" = "https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/blob/release/CHANGELOG.md"

[tool.ty]

[tool.ty.src]
include = ["benchbox", "tests"]
exclude = ["tests/fixtures", "**/__pycache__"]

[tool.ty.rules]

too-many-positional-arguments = "error"
conflicting-declarations = "error"
invalid-parameter-default = "error"
unresolved-reference = "error"
not-iterable = "error"

unresolved-attribute = "ignore"
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"
invalid-assignment = "ignore"
unsupported-operator = "ignore"
invalid-method-override = "ignore"
not-subscriptable = "ignore"
call-non-callable = "ignore"

unresolved-import = "warn"
invalid-return-type = "warn"
invalid-type-form = "warn"
no-matching-overload = "warn"
unknown-argument = "warn"
missing-argument = "warn"

possibly-unresolved-reference = "warn"
possibly-missing-attribute = "warn"

[tool.ty.terminal]
error-on-warning = false

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "ruff==0.16.7",
    "ty>=0.0.1a14",
    "duckdb>=1.5.0,<2.0.0",
    "polars>=1.35.2",
    "clickhouse-connect>=0.10.0",
    "psycopg[binary]>=3.1",
    "pytest>=8.0.0",
    "pytest-cov>=6.2.1",
    "pytest-benchmark>=5.1.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.4.0",
    "pandas>=3.0.0",
    "pyiceberg[sql-sqlite,pyarrow]>=0.10.0",
    "deltalake>=1.2.1",
    "datafusion>=54.0.0",
    "cloudpathlib[s3,gs,azure]>=0.15.0",
    "chdb>=0.10.0; sys_platform != 'win32'",
    "clickhouse-driver>=0.2.0",
    "trino>=0.336.0",
    "firebolt-sdk>=1.18.0",
    "influxdb3-python>=0.10.0",
    "databricks-sdk>=0.20.0",
    "pyspark>=3.5.0",
    "mcp>=2,<3",
    "mutmut>=3.5.0",
    "dask[distributed]>=2026.1.1",
    "pymysql>=1.1.2",
    "delta-spark>=4.1.0",
    "presto-python-client>=0.8.4",
    "codespell>=2.4.2",
    "pre-commit>=4.6.0",
    "import-linter>=2.13",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.44,<2",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http>=1.44,<2",
    "pytest-json-report>=1.5.0",
    "pygments>=2.18.0",
    "markdown-it-py>=4.0.0",
    "bashlex==0.18",
    "lxml>=6.0.0",
]

[tool.mutmut]
paths_to_mutate = [
    "benchbox/platforms/duckdb.py",
    "benchbox/platforms/base/adapter.py",
    "benchbox/core/runner/runner.py",
    "benchbox/core/visualization/chart_generator.py",
    "benchbox/cli/commands/run.py",
]
tests_dir = ["tests/unit/"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"benchbox._vendor" = ["*.zip", "sqlglot.json", "SQLGLOT_LICENSE.txt"]
"benchbox.core" = ["benchmark_registry.yaml"]
"benchbox.core.equivalence" = ["cross_surface_baseline.yaml"]
"benchbox.core.flightdata" = ["query_catalog.yaml"]
"benchbox.core.nyctaxi" = ["query_catalog.yaml"]
"benchbox.core.results" = ["benchmark_specs.yaml"]
"benchbox.core.primitives.catalog" = ["queries.yaml"]
"benchbox.core.tsbs_devops" = ["query_catalog.yaml"]
"benchbox.data.coffeeshop" = ["*.csv"]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py311"
exclude = [
    "migrations",
    "venv",
    ".git",
    "__pycache__",
    ".tox",
    "examples/notebooks",
    "examples/visualization",
    "tests/validation",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
preview = true
select = [
    "E",
    "W",
    "F",
    "I",
    "N",
    "UP",
    "B",
    "C4",
    "C90",
    "PIE",
    "SIM",
    "PLW1514",
    "TID251",
]
ignore = [
    "E501",
    "E402",
    "E721",
    "E731",
    "E741",
    "B905",
    "B007",
    "B017",
    "B023",

    "B027",

]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"sqlglot".msg = "Use the bundled wheel runtime through benchbox._vendor.sqlglot."

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
force-single-line = false
combine-as-imports = true
known-first-party = ["benchbox", "_project"]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 18

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"benchbox/core/tpcds/schema/registry.py" = ["F405"]
"tests/**/conftest.py" = ["F401", "F811"]
"tests/**/test_*.py" = ["F401", "F811"]
"**/__init__.py" = ["F401", "F811", "F822"]
"benchbox/utils/runtime_env.py" = ["F401"]
"_project/sqlglot-upstream/repros/repro_all.py" = ["TID251"]
"_project/sqlglot-upstream/repros/sqlite_extract.py" = ["TID251"]
"_project/scripts/build_joinorder_data.py" = ["TID251"]
"tests/utilities/qgen_wrapper.py" = ["TID251"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
line-ending = "auto"
exclude = ["*.md"]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["benchbox"]
branch = true
omit = [
    "benchbox/__main__.py",
    "**/test_*.py",
    "**/conftest.py",
    "benchbox/core/tpcds/dataframe_queries/queries.py",
    "benchbox/core/tpcds/dataframe_queries/rollup_helper.py",
    "benchbox/core/tpcds/dataframe_queries/channel_helper.py",
    "benchbox/core/datavault/dataframe_queries/queries.py",
    "benchbox/core/nyctaxi/dataframe_queries/queries.py",
    "benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/scd_processor.py",
    "benchbox/experimental/load_testing/executor.py",
    "benchbox/experimental/load_testing/pool_tester.py",
    "benchbox/core/clickbench/dataframe_queries/queries.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "@abstractmethod",
]


[tool.benchbox.complexity]
max_complexity = 18
warn_complexity = 12
max_exception_days = 90
exclusions = []

source_root = "benchbox"

# Output and behavior
addopts = [
    "-v",                        # Verbose output
    "--strict-markers",          # Treat unregistered markers as errors
    "--tb=short",                # Shorter traceback format
    "--cov=middleware",          # Enable coverage for middleware packages
    "--cov-report=term-missing", # Show missing lines in terminal
    "--cov-report=html",         # Generate HTML coverage report
    "--cov-report=xml",          # Generate XML coverage report (for CI)
    "--cov-fail-under=80",       # Fail if coverage is below 80%
]

# Asyncio mode
asyncio_mode = "auto"

# Custom markers
markers = [
    "asyncio: marks tests as async",
    "unit: marks tests as unit tests",
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
    "system_local: marks tests that use locally runnable external services (e.g. testcontainers)",
    "system_external: marks tests that depend on real external systems/secrets",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
# Coverage measurement settings
source = ["middleware"]
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/.venv/*",
    "*/venv/*",
    "*/.pytest_cache/*",
    "*/build/*",
    "*/dist/*",
    "*/*.egg-info/*",
]
branch = true  # Measure branch coverage

[tool.coverage.report]
# Coverage reporting settings
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@abstractmethod",
    "@abc.abstractmethod",
]

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"
# CI docker tags look like `{id}-docker-v1.1.1` or
# `{id}-docker-v1.1.1-introduce-report-lib.4`. The branch suffix after
# X.Y.Z is GitVersion SemVer, not PEP 440 — hatch-vcs rejects it. Capture
# only the numeric triple (same rationale as docker/Dockerfile.sql_to_arc).
tag-pattern = '^(?:\d+-docker-)?(?P<version>[vV]?\d+\.\d+\.\d+)(?:-.*)?$'

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
include = ["README.md"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Keep this ruleset architecture-focused and low-noise:
# - import hygiene/boundaries (`I`, `TID`)

# - risky exception handling (`BLE`)
# - avoid ad-hoc print debugging in app code (`T20`)

[tool.uv]
cache-keys = [{ file = "pyproject.toml" }, { git = { commit = true, tags = true } }]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
strict = true
exclude = ["^references/", "^tmp/"]
ignore_missing_imports = true
local_partial_types = true
warn_unreachable = true
enable_error_code = [
    "truthy-bool",
    "truthy-iterable",
    "redundant-expr",
    "unused-awaitable",
    "ignore-without-code",
    "possibly-undefined",
    "redundant-self",
    "unimported-reveal",
    "deprecated",
    "exhaustive-match",
]
disable_error_code = [
    "unused-ignore",
    "no-any-return",
]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["tests.*"]
strict = false
disable_error_code = ["valid-type", "misc", "untyped-decorator", "attr-defined"]

[tool.pyright]
include = ["src/acodex", "tests"]
exclude = ["references", "tmp", ".venv"]
pythonVersion = "3.11"
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"
typeCheckingMode = "basic"
strict = ["src/acodex"]
reportUnknownMemberType = false
reportUnknownArgumentType = false
reportUnknownVariableType = false
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
reportPrivateUsage = false

[tool.pyrefly]
project-includes = ["src/acodex", "tests"]
project-excludes = ["references", "tmp", ".venv"]
preset = "strict"
min-severity = "warn"

[tool.pyrefly.errors]
implicit-any-attribute = false
implicit-any-empty-container = false
missing-attribute = false
missing-override-decorator = false
unused-ignore = true

[tool.slotscheck]
strict-imports = false
exclude-classes = '''
(
  :.*Error
  |:.*Exception
  |acodex\.config\..*:.*Config
  |acodex\.config\.models:.*Config
  |acodex\.core\.codex_app\.bridge:CodexAppBridgeSettings
  |acodex\.core\.codex_app\.cdp\.settings:CodexCDPSettings
)
'''

[tool.codespell]
skip = [
    "__pycache__",
    "_build",
    ".mypy_cache",
    "*.lock",
    "references/**",
    "tmp/**",
]

[tool.typos.files]
extend-exclude = [
    "__pycache__",
    "_build",
    ".mypy_cache",
    "*.lock",
    "references/**",
    "tmp/**",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["."]
addopts = [
    "-ra",
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
]
markers = [
    "real_integration: opt-in tests that exercise a live local Codex CLI setup",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "error",
    # Ignore ResourceWarnings from unclosed sockets/event loops during GC

    "ignore:unclosed <socket.socket:ResourceWarning",
    "ignore:unclosed event loop:ResourceWarning",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/acodex"]
branch = true
parallel = true

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 100
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@overload",
    "@typing.overload",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "\\.\\.\\.",
]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true

noClasses()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..domain..")
                .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..application..")
                .because("the domain layer is the innermost ring and must not depend on the application layer")
                .check(allClasses);

noClasses()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..domain..")
                .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..")
                .because("the domain layer must stay free of adapter concerns")
                .check(allClasses);

noClasses()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..application..")
                .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..")
                .because("application services should orchestrate ports instead of depending on adapters directly")
                .check(allClasses);

noClasses()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..inbound..")
                .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..outbound..")
                .because("inbound adapters must communicate through ports instead of reaching into outbound adapters")
                .check(allClasses);

noClasses()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..outbound..")
                .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..inbound..")
                .because("outbound adapters must not depend on inbound adapter implementation details")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..domain..model..")
                .and().areNotEnums()
                .and().areNotInterfaces()
                .and().areNotAnonymousClasses()
                .should().beAssignableTo(Record.class)
                .because("hexagon domain models should be immutable records unless they are enums or closed interfaces")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..domain..model..")
                .should().notBeAnnotatedWith(JAKARTA_PERSISTENCE_ANNOTATION)
                .because("jakarta.persistence annotations are adapter concerns and must not leak into hexagon domain models")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..application..port..inbound..")
                .and().areInterfaces()
                .should().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("UseCase")
                .because("inbound port interfaces represent use case contracts and should end with UseCase")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..application..port..inbound..")
                .and().areNotInterfaces()
                .should().beAssignableTo(Record.class)
                .because("supporting types in inbound port packages should be immutable records")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..domain..port..outbound..")
                .should().beInterfaces()
                .because("outbound ports define contracts that adapters implement")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..application..")
                .and(IMPLEMENTS_USE_CASE_INTERFACE)
                .should().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Service")
                .because("hexagon use case implementations should follow the Service naming convention")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..application..")
                .and(IMPLEMENTS_USE_CASE_INTERFACE)
                .should().beAnnotatedWith(ApplicationScoped.class)
                .because("hexagon use case implementations should be exposed as application-scoped beans")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..")

                .should().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..outbound..")
                .because("hexagon JPA entities must be confined to outbound adapters")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..outbound..")
                .and().areAnnotatedWith(Entity.class)

                .check(allClasses);

classes()

classes()

noClasses()

classes()

[tool.bandit]

  "benchmarks",
  "examples",
  "scripts",

]
skips = [
  "B101"
]

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"
skip_covered = false
skip_empty = false

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
  "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
  "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
  "def __repr__",
  "if 0:",
  "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
  "if self.debug:",
  "if settings.DEBUG",
  "pass",
  "pragma: no cover",
  "raise AssertionError",
  "raise ImportError",
  "raise NotImplementedError"
]
fail_under = 80
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
omit = [
  "*/__pycache__/*",
  "*/conftest.py",
  "*/examples/*",
  "*/scripts/*",
  "*/tests/*"
]
parallel = true
source = ["src"]

[tool.coverage.xml]
output = "coverage.xml"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
include = [
  "LICENSE",
  "README.md",
  "pyproject.toml",
  "src/calibrax"
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/calibrax"]

[tool.hatch.version]
path = "src/calibrax/__init__.py"

[tool.interrogate]
exclude = ["examples", "scripts", "tests"]
fail-under = 80
ignore-init-method = true
ignore-init-module = false
ignore-magic = true

[tool.pydoclint]
allow-init-docstring = true
arg-type-hints-in-docstring = false
# Instance attributes are documented under Attributes per the Google style; pydoclint would
# compare them with class-level attributes only.
check-class-attributes = false
# Annotations are the source of truth for types; docstrings carry the prose.
check-return-types = false
check-yield-types = false
# `# noqa: DOC...` is read from the def line, where propagated exceptions are annotated.
native-mode-noqa-location = "definition"
style = "google"

[tool.pylint."messages_control"]
max-args = 10
max-attributes = 12

[tool.pyright]
exclude = [
  "examples",
  "scripts"
]
include = [
  "src",
  "tests"
]
pythonVersion = "3.12"
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
typeCheckingMode = "standard"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "--strict-markers --strict-config --verbose --tb=short --color=yes --durations=10 --disable-warnings --cov=src/calibrax --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=html --cov-fail-under=80 --timeout=300 --json-report --json-report-file=temp/test-results.json --json-report-indent=2"
cache_dir = ".pytest_cache"
console_output_style = "progress"
filterwarnings = [
  "ignore:.*CUDA-enabled jaxlib.*",
  "ignore:.*cuSPARSE.*",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:jax.*",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:pkg_resources.*",
  "ignore::UserWarning:jax._src.xla_bridge",
  "ignore:jax.interpreters.xla.pytype_aval_mappings is deprecated:DeprecationWarning"
]
log_cli = true
log_cli_level = "INFO"
markers = [
  "benchmark: marks tests as performance benchmarks (requires pytest-benchmark)",
  "contract: marks tests as contract tests",
  "cpu: marks tests that should run on CPU only",
  "cuda: marks tests that specifically test CUDA functionality",
  "doctest: marks tests as documentation example tests",
  "e2e: marks tests as end-to-end tests",
  "gpu: marks tests that require GPU (deselect with '-m \"not gpu\"')",
  "gpu_required: marks tests as requiring GPU (will fail if GPU unavailable)",
  "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
  "performance: marks tests as performance tests (alias for benchmark)",
  "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
  "unit: marks tests as unit tests"
]
minversion = "6.0"
python_classes = "Test*"
python_files = "test_*.py"
python_functions = "test_*"
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.pytest_env]
JAX_PLATFORMS = {skip_if_set = true, value = "cpu"}
MPLBACKEND = {skip_if_set = true, value = "Agg"}
TF_CPP_MIN_LOG_LEVEL = {skip_if_set = true, value = "1"}

[tool.ruff]
extend-include = ["*.ipynb"]
line-length = 100
# First-party modules come from src/ and the isort settings only, so an untracked directory at the
# repository root (wandb's run logs are ./wandb) cannot make a third-party package first-party.
src = ["src"]
target-version = "py312"

[tool.ruff.format]
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "auto"
quote-style = "double"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false

[tool.ruff.lint]
# pydoclint's codes, so a `# noqa: DOC...` is not reported as unknown.
external = ["DOC"]
fixable = [
  "E",
  "F",
  "F401",
  "F841",
  "I001",
  "W",
  "W291",
  "W292",
  "W293"
]
ignore = [
  # Google-style docstrings: D203 and D213 conflict with D211 and D212.
  "D203",
  "D213",
  # The formatter owns line length.
  "E501",
  # The __all__ lists are grouped by domain with comments; a sort would destroy the grouping.
  "RUF022",
  # Exception messages are written inline; a message class per raise is noise.
  "TRY003"
]
select = [
  "ANN",
  "ARG",
  "B",
  "C4",
  "C90",
  "D",
  "E",
  "F",
  "I",
  "N",
  "PIE",
  "PL",
  "PT",
  "PTH",
  "RET",
  "RUF",
  "S",
  "SIM",
  "T20",
  "TRY",
  "UP",
  "W"
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
combine-as-imports = true
known-first-party = ["calibrax", "tests"]
lines-after-imports = 2
order-by-type = false

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Examples are narrative walkthroughs: they print, and their main functions are long.
"examples/*" = ["C901", "PLR0915", "T20"]
# Development scripts report on stdout.
"scripts/*" = ["T20"]
# The CLI's output is print by design.
"src/calibrax/cli/*" = ["T201"]
# Test factories are keyword-only builders with one parameter per field.
"tests/*" = ["D", "PLR0913", "PLR2004", "S101"]
# Local stubs for untyped libraries spell names as the library does (NVML's camelCase).
"typings/*" = ["N"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-args = 8

[tool.substrax.compute]
backend = "modal"

[tool.substrax.compute.backends.modal]
outputs_volume = "calibrax-example-outputs"

[tool.substrax.compute.jobs.examples]
accelerator = {kind = "L4"}
examples = ["examples/metrics"]
extras = ["cuda12"]
runtime = {platforms = ["cuda"], preallocate = false, xla_flags = ["--xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true"]}
task_timeout_seconds = 1800

[tool.uv]
# calibrax does not import optax; flax does. Below 0.2.8 optax calls
# jax.config.update("jax_pmap_shmap_merge"), which jax removed in 0.10, so importing
# flax raises AttributeError and takes out collection for the whole suite. Constrained
# rather than declared, because this is a transitive requirement, not a direct one.
constraint-dependencies = ["optax>=0.2.8"]

[tool.uv.pip]

# `packages` discovery — Hatch walks the package tree and includes all files,
# not just .py. The earlier explicit `force-include` of the templates
# directory caused PyPI to reject the wheel with "Duplicate filename in local
# headers" because the same files landed twice (once via packages, once via
# force-include). Keep it out — packages alone is correct.

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow",
    "integration: marks tests requiring external services",

    "benchmark: performance budget tests (spec §8.5)",
]
filterwarnings = [
    # starlette uses deprecated multipart import — third-party, can't fix
    "ignore::PendingDeprecationWarning:starlette",
    # asyncio transport cleanup after event loop is closed (Windows + Linux)
    "ignore:Exception ignored in.*Transport:pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning",

    "ignore:coroutine .* was never awaited:RuntimeWarning",
]

src = ["src", "tests"]
# Crew scaffolder templates are Jinja2 source trees, not Python packages —
# they use ``{{ project_name }}`` in directory/file names and ship ``.jinja``
# templates that aren't valid Python until rendered.
extend-exclude = ["src/cognithor/crew/templates"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "W", "F", "I", "N", "UP", "B", "SIM", "TCH", "RUF",
]
ignore = [
    "RUF001",  # Ambiguous EN DASH in strings (korrekt im Deutschen)
    "RUF002",  # Ambiguous EN DASH in docstrings
    "RUF003",  # Ambiguous EN DASH in comments
    "RUF012",  # Mutable class defaults — dataclass pattern, harmless
    "N806",    # Non-lowercase variable in function — Windows API constants
    "N801",    # Invalid class name — test naming conventions
    "N802",    # Invalid function name — intentional conventions
    "N805",    # Invalid first argument name — intentional
    "N811",    # Constant imported as non-constant — intentional
    "N814",    # Camelcase imported as constant — intentional
    "N818",    # Error suffix on exception name — intentional
    "E402",    # Module import not at top — conditional imports by design
    "E741",    # Ambiguous variable name — l, O, I in math code
    "SIM117",  # Multiple with statements — style preference only
    "SIM103",  # Needless bool — style preference
    "SIM108",  # If-else-block instead of if-exp — readability preference
    "SIM112",  # Uncapitalized env vars — intentional
    "SIM115",  # Open file with context handler — controlled usage
    "B027",    # Empty method without abstract decorator — intentional pattern
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]  # Re-exports in __init__.py are intentional
"tests/test_install_fixes.py" = ["E501"]  # Embedded shell/JS scripts in strings
"tests/test_packs/test_installer.py" = ["TC003"]  # Path used in runtime test bodies via pytest fixtures

"src/cognithor/crew/compiler_hierarchical.py" = ["TC001"]  # CrewAgent/CrewTask used at runtime in pure-function signatures
"src/cognithor/crew/crew.py" = ["TC001"]  # CrewAgent/CrewTask/CrewProcess must be imported at runtime for Pydantic validation
# Hardware-Aware Runtime: dataclasses + manifest models are accessed at runtime
# (e.g. `manifest.tiers` iteration, `Solution.blockers` access). Ruff's TC001

# `scripts/gen_state_types.py` generator import it; `state_schema.py` is never
# imported on the live request path.

# `scripts/run_consumer_contracts.py` validates the real producer artifacts
# against consumer-authored expectations. Like `pydantic`, it is DEV/CI-only and
# must NEVER enter the runtime `dependencies` above — core stays zero-runtime-dep.

    "pydantic>=2.13,<3",
    # Dev/build-only — drives the MOR-883 consumer-driven contract runner.

    "hypothesis>=6.0",

# Codegen-only contract schema (MOR-881). Under the global ``follow_imports =

# rather than wiring the pydantic mypy plugin into the strict web boundary.

[tool.mutmut]
# Weekly mutation-testing trend job. The whole src/ tree is
# copied into mutants/ so imports stay intact; only_mutate restricts
# mutation to the small high-risk modules of the stabilization program.
source_paths = ["src/"]
# Top-level test-support and rig-profile data; without these the copied
# tree cannot import rigplane_testkit (pythonpath=["."]) or discover any

# ── Permanent policy ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# reportPrivateUsage: Python's _name is a convention (advisory), not access
# control. Pyright enforcing it generates false positives on tightly-coupled
# partner modules, stdlib internals, and white-box test access — none of which
# represent real violations. Enforced by code review, not by the type checker.
reportPrivateUsage = "none"
#
# reportUnusedFunction: Decorator-registered callables (Discord app_commands,
# Telegram update handlers, asyncio task targets) are not statically reachable.
# Confirmed by manual audit 2026-03-23: all 48 src hits are dynamic registrations
# or private module helpers called through the module's public entry point.
reportUnusedFunction = "none"
# ── Wave 4 (#411) — config loading migrated to Pydantic ──────────────────────
# Rules still suppressed: cascading errors from non-config dict[str, Any] in
# business logic, LLM drivers, and tests (~3,165 hits total). Config sites
# are now fully typed. Re-enable incrementally in follow-up issues.
reportUnknownVariableType = "none"
reportUnknownMemberType = "none"
reportUnknownArgumentType = "none"
reportUnknownParameterType = "none"
reportMissingParameterType = "none"
reportUnknownLambdaType = "none"
reportMissingTypeArgument = "none"

[project]
name = "tg-agent"
version = "0.2.4.1"
description = "Telegram automation dependency for coding agents — tg-agent CLI + skill for Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex"
readme = "README.md"
license = "MIT"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [
    {name = "Axisrow"}
]
keywords = ["telegram", "agent", "automation", "assistant", "telethon", "content"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Environment :: Console",
    "Environment :: Web Environment",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Topic :: Communications :: Chat",
]
dependencies = [
    "telethon>=1.43.2",
    "telethon-floodgate>=0.1.2,<0.2",
    "telethon-cli>=0.1.1",
    # Telethon's SOCKS/HTTP proxy path (TG_PROXY) needs python-socks with the
    # asyncio extra; without it Telethon silently ignores `proxy=` (warns only).
    "python-socks[asyncio]>=2.0",
    # Live dialog history reads (`dialogs read` / GET /dialogs/history, #1234
    # follow-up) reuse tg_messenger's StandaloneTelegramClient.history() for its
    # model mapping and flood-wait retry — see tg_agent/telegram/dm_history.py for why
    # it never opens a second connection. Note its per-instance history TTL cache
    # does NOT apply here: we build a throwaway client per call, so every read
    # hits Telegram. Caching happens one level up, in runtime_snapshots.
    "tg-messenger>=0.1.0",
    "fastapi>=0.136.3,<0.144",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.48.0",
    "jinja2>=3.1.6",
    "aiosqlite>=0.22.1",
    "apscheduler>=3.11.3",
    "pydantic>=2.13.4",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.14.1",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.3",
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.2",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.29",
    # CLI framework (epic #959, argparse→Typer migration). Typer was already in
    # the tree transitively; pinning it directly makes the dependency explicit
    # for the Wave-0 scaffold (tg_agent/cli/typer_app.py). 0.12 is the first release
    # with the modern click 8.x API the scaffold relies on.
    "typer>=0.12.0",
    "cryptography>=48.0.0",
    "openpyxl>=3.1.5",
    "aiohttp>=3.13.5",
    "numpy>=2.4.6",
    "scikit-learn>=1.8.0",
    "jieba>=0.42.1",
    "langdetect>=1.0.9",
    "textual[syntax]>=8.2.8",
    "claude-agent-sdk>=0.2.87",
    "deepagents>=0.6.4",
    "huggingface_hub>=1.16.4",
    # Image-generation SDKs (issue #958): the OpenAI/Together/Replicate image
    # adapters use these instead of raw aiohttp. ``openai`` was already in the
    # tree transitively via ``langchain-openai``; pinning it directly makes the
    # dependency explicit. Together's images endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, so it
    # reuses the ``openai`` SDK with a custom ``base_url`` (no heavy ``together``
    # SDK). ``replicate`` is lightweight (httpx + pydantic, both already present)
    # and removes the hand-rolled prediction-polling loop. HuggingFace stays on
    # raw aiohttp on purpose — its SDK returns a PIL.Image (a Pillow dependency)
    # whereas the raw path saves the image/* bytes directly.
    # openai 3.x adopted (the deliberate revisit the #1300 cap promised): 3.x
    # replaced the default httpx transport with the httpx2 package, so every
    # httpx.Client/AsyncClient monkeypatch in the test suite silently misses —
    # tests stop mocking the real request and hit the live provider. The
    # interception tests now patch BOTH httpx and httpx2 (guarded import), so
    # 2.x and 3.x stay sealed.
    "openai>=3.19.2,<4",
    "replicate>=1.0.7",
    "langchain>=1.3.2",
    "langchain-core>=1.4.0",
    "langchain-ollama>=1.1.0",
    "langchain-openai>=1.2.2",
    "tenacity>=9.1.4",
    "pybreaker>=1.4.0",
    "httpx>=0.28.1",
    "beautifulsoup4>=4.14.3",
    "orjson>=3.10.0",
    "itsdangerous>=2.2.0",
    # ReDoS guard for user-supplied notification regexes: the `regex` engine's
    # `timeout=` aborts catastrophic backtracking inside its C matching loop,
    # which the stdlib `re` cannot (#1240). Present transitively (dateparser,
    # tiktoken) but declared here because it is now a direct runtime import.
    "regex>=2024.11.6",
    # QR login in the web panel (#1551): renders the tg://login token as an
    # inline SVG (SvgPathImage) — no PIL pull, unlike the PNG factories.
    "qrcode>=8.0",
]

# Static security analysis config for `bandit -c pyproject.toml -r tg_agent` (#1053).
# The CI step (static-checks) runs it advisory (continue-on-error) for now; this
# scopes the scan to tg_agent/ and skips the test tree. Findings are triaged into a
# skip-list / `# nosec` here before the step is ever made blocking.
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests"]

# Dead-code scan whitelist (vulture, #1136). vulture auto-reads this section,
# so it applies both to `python -m vulture tg_agent/` and to scripts/code_health.py.
# Every name here is a VERIFIED false-positive — do not delete the code it
# refers to; each entry must say why it is intentionally "unused".
[tool.vulture]
ignore_names = [
    # tg_agent/utils/json.py safe_json_dumps(ensure_ascii=...): intentional
    # call-site-compatibility parameter after the orjson migration (#956) —
    # orjson is always UTF-8, the flag is accepted so existing
    # `safe_json_dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=True)` calls don't break, but has
    # no effect. Removing it would break call sites. See issue #1136.
    "ensure_ascii",
]

# Doc-coverage (interrogate, #1072). scripts/doc_coverage.py and the advisory
# CI step read this. `fail_under` is a SOFT baseline — a ratchet floor that
# surfaces regressions without forcing a docstring-everything sprint. Raise it
# as coverage climbs. interrogate ignores things that don't need a docstring
# (magic/init/nested/private, overloads).
# Ratchet history: 23 (#1072 floor) → 35 (#1134: documented the public-API
# facade — tg_agent/models.py Pydantic models, db.repos bundles, repository CRUD —
# lifting coverage 27% → 40.6%; floor set to 35 to lock in the win with a
# margin below the measured 40.6% so a stray docstring loss doesn't trip the
# gate). Doc-coverage is NOT a CI gate (#1097) — stays a local script.
[tool.interrogate]
fail_under = 35
ignore_init_method = true
ignore_init_module = true
ignore_magic = true
ignore_nested_functions = true
ignore_private = true
ignore_semiprivate = true
ignore_property_decorators = true
ignore_overloaded_functions = true
exclude = ["tests", "scripts", "build", "dist", "site", "mutants"]
verbose = 1

# Mutation testing (mutmut 3.8). Root-caused 07.10.26: stock mutmut is
# incompatible with a FLAT layout whose import package is literally named
# `src` (as this repo's was before the #1448 rename to tg_agent) — it strips a
# `src.` prefix from module names (breaking the trampoline routing and stats
# keys) and asserts against `src.`-prefixed trampoline hits. With the rename
# stock mutmut works again; the strip_src_prefix knob stays until the upstream
# PR (boxed/mutmut, branch fix/strip-src-prefix-knob) lands on PyPI — the fork
# is installed editable from its local checkout. The sandbox ships
# everything tests read outside tg_agent/tests, both at collection time (root
# conftest.py, scripts/) and at run time (.github/workflows/ci.yml,
# docs/reference/*, adk/). data/ is deliberately NOT copied — it holds the
# live DB; sandbox tests run on tmp/in-memory databases. mutmut never prunes
# a stale sandbox (deleted files keep their old copies) — `rm -rf mutants`
# before a rerun.
[tool.mutmut]
source_paths = ["tg_agent"]
also_copy = [
    "conftest.py",
    "scripts",
    ".github/workflows",
    "docs/reference",
    "adk",
    "mkdocs.yml",
    "config.yaml",
    "docker-compose.yml",
]
strip_src_prefix = false
# The fork-isolated serial stats phase pushes the whole suite (~10.7k tests,
# collect-verified 08.10.26) serially through one process; full sandbox runs
# have not completed yet, so the observations are from partial runs: leaky
# leftovers from earlier tests (unclosed sqlite connections, destroyed-pending
# asyncio tasks) get finalized mid-run, and pytest's unraisable AND
# threadexception plugins attribute each to whichever test happens to run
# (seen at 1713 and 3673 green tests respectively) — both plugins are
# disabled for mutation runs; the normal suite still enforces strictness in
# CI. Known cost: a mutant whose only observable effect is a
# broken cleanup path (unclosed connection, uncancelled task) now survives
# silently — the score overstates resource-lifecycle code; such survivors
# need a manual look.
pytest_add_cli_args = [
    "-p", "no:unraisableexception",
    "-p", "no:threadexception",
    "-m", "not mutmut_skip",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
exclude = ["graqle/benchmarks/data/*", "paper/*", "patent/*"]

[tool.hatch.build]
artifacts = [
    "graqle/integrations/bridges/*.md",
    "graqle/docs/*.md",  # T09 (v0.51.6): ship MCP tool inventory in wheel
    # P1 (ADR-222): ship the governance constitution single-source-of-truth so
    # `graq init` renders the full rulebook into CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/etc. Without
    # this the .md fragments are stripped from the wheel and init silently falls
    # back to the abridged inline copy. Owner-approved (harish, 2026-06-07).
    # V-CR-GOV-INSTALL-P1-NATIVE-001: graq_edit G4 + graq_config_audit could not
    # resolve the worktree path (S-010 class); native edit with recorded approval.
    "graqle/data/constitution/*.md",
    # ed25519 cutover (ADR-215 §5): the Community trust source — PUBLIC licence
    # signing keys so offline installs can verify v2 licences. Public-key-only
    # (the private signer is server-side; keygen.py is excluded below).
    "graqle/licensing/trusted_keys.json",
    # CR-010.R1: the frozen proof spec + its conformance corpus. These MUST ship
    # in the wheel — the whole point is that a third party can implement a
    # conformant verifier from the published schemas + golden vectors alone.
    # Loaded via importlib.resources (never __file__), so they resolve from a
    # zip-imported wheel. Spec version is decoupled from the SDK version.
    "graqle/pct/schema/proof-spec/**/*.json",
    "graqle/pct/schema/proof-spec/**/*.md",
    "graqle/pct/schema/conformance/*.json",
    "graqle/pct/schema/conformance/fixtures/*",
    # CR-010.R3: compliance packs are DATA — a framework is a pack.yaml plus a
    # schema.json, so adding NIST AI RMF / ISO 42001 needs no Python. These MUST
    # ship in the wheel or the packs silently vanish from an installed SDK and
    # only first-party imports keep working. Loaded via importlib.resources
    # (never Path(__file__).parents[N], which resolves elsewhere once installed).
    "graqle/compliance/packs/**/*.yaml",
    "graqle/compliance/packs/**/*.json",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["graqle"]
exclude = [
    "graqle/benchmarks/data/*",
    # B3/S2: shapes.ttl excluded from wheel — structural SHACL logic is
    # readable even with opaque URNs; keep it server-side only until ADR-206
    # documents accepted disclosure posture before public PyPI.
    "graqle/governance/shacl/shapes.ttl",
    # WS-C C1 (ADR-BIZ-001): the Community (Apache-2.0) wheel ships WITHOUT the
    # proprietary commercial backends. These live in the source tree but are
    # carved out of the public wheel; the proprietary graqle-studio /
    # graqle-enterprise distributions re-include them. The thin cli/commands/*
    # wrappers ship and degrade gracefully (graqle/cli/_edition_guard.py) when a
    # backend is absent. An import-direction CI gate enforces that no Community
    # module eagerly imports these (lazy-only invariant). scorch + phantom are
    # NON-CORE plugins and intentionally REMAIN in Community (Harish, 2026-06-01).
    "graqle/cloud/*",
    "graqle/leads/*",
    "graqle/studio/*",
    "graqle/server/*",
    # WS-D D-pkg (ADR-BIZ-001): the admin licence SIGNER must not ship in the
    # public Community wheel. keygen.py embeds the legacy HMAC signing secret
    # (its own docstring: "never distribute to end users"); generate_key signs
    # licences. With ed25519 (WS-D) the wheel verifies with a PUBLIC key only and
    # cannot forge, but excluding the signer is belt-and-suspenders — the public
    # artifact carries verification, never issuance.
    "graqle/licensing/keygen.py",
    # WS-F (ADR-BIZ-001): trade-secret calibration internals — TS-1..TS-4
    # implementation details (weights, AGREEMENT_THRESHOLD, J̄ formula, θ_fold
    # derivation, STG production rules). The Community wheel ships the public
    # interface (output scores, status enums) but never the computation internals.
    # The trade-secret wheel gate (scripts/ci/trade_secret_wheel_gate.py) enforces
    # this mechanically on every PR and release build.
    "graqle/governance/calibration.py",
    "graqle/governance/calibration_store.py",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
# NOTE: graqle/data/claude_gate is covered by packages=["graqle"] above.
# Adding a force-include for a path already under the packages tree
# creates duplicate local-header entries in the wheel ZIP and causes
# PyPI to reject the upload with HTTP 400 "Duplicate filename in
# local headers". Only force-include paths OUTSIDE the packages tree.
"examples" = "graqle/examples"

    { include = "CortexOS" },
    { include = "packs" },
    { include = "cortex_contract", from = "packages" }

# pip resolves [project].dependencies. Do not reintroduce a caret table here —
# it silently capped cryptography at <43 and pillow at <11. See
# tests/packaging/test_dependency_floors.py.

[tool.poetry.extras]
agentic = ["dbos"]
rag = ["sentence-transformers", "qdrant-client", "tantivy"]
full = ["dbos", "sentence-transformers", "qdrant-client", "tantivy"]
dev = ["pytest", "pytest-asyncio", "respx", "ruff", "mypy", "import-linter", "types-PyYAML"]
local-inference = ["llama-cpp-python"]
gpu = ["torch", "llama-cpp-python"]
a2a = ["websockets"]
personality = []
postgres = ["sqlalchemy", "asyncpg", "psycopg"]
agents = ["dbos"]
tokens = ["tiktoken"]
api = []
dms = []

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B"]
ignore = ["E501", "B008"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
ignore_missing_imports = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
check_untyped_defs = false
pretty = true
# The contract package is distributed as top-level `cortex_contract`. Without
# this, mypy resolves packages/cortex_contract/*.py as both `cortex_contract.*`
# (the __init__.py walk-up) and `packages.cortex_contract.*` (as a namespace
# package from the root) and refuses to run at all.
mypy_path = "packages"
namespace_packages = false
# A setuptools build/ tree under the package is a *copy* of it, so mypy sees two
# modules named cortex_contract and stops with "errors prevented further
# checking" — exit 2, nothing type-checked, and it reads like an environment
# glitch rather than a disabled gate. Any `pip install -e .` or `python -m
# build` recreates it, so excluding it is the fix; deleting it is not.
exclude = '(^|/)build/'
# Packaging / release infra only — engine modules remain gradually typed.
files = [
    "CortexOS/packaging.py",
    "packages/cortex_contract",
    "scripts/check_versions.py",
    "scripts/export_openapi.py",
    "scripts/export_semantics.py",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["."]
markers = [
    "corpus_expanded: full paraphrase expansion (slow; set CORPUS_EXPANDED=1)",
]

[project]
name = "bernstein"
version = "3.22.0"
description = "The open-source governance layer for AI agents. No model in the coordination loop, so replaying a plan reproduces its task graph byte-identically, and run receipts are byte-identical across independent builds. Signed lineage plus an opt-in HMAC audit chain a reviewer checks offline, without rerunning it. Runs Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and 40+ CLI agents; governs any deliverable from code to research to audit evidence packs. Cluster mode, air-gap deploy."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
license = "Apache-2.0"
authors = [{ name = "Alex Chernysh", email = "alex@alexchernysh.com" }]
keywords = [
    "ai",
    "agents",
    "orchestration",
    "multi-agent",
    "coding",
    "cli",
    "llm",
    "automation",
    "devtools",
    "deterministic",
    "replay",
    "audit",
    "provenance",
    "lineage",
    "worktree",
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: System Administrators",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Operating System :: POSIX :: Linux",
    "Operating System :: MacOS",
    "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows",
    "Programming Language :: Python",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Software Development",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Build Tools",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Code Generators",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Quality Assurance",
    "Topic :: System :: Distributed Computing",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
dependencies = [
    # No ceiling: the route-table walk that the agent task-scope gate compiles
    # its matchers from lives in ``core/routes/route_table.py`` and descends
    # through the ``include_router`` wrappers FastAPI keeps from 0.137 onward,
    # so it resolves the same templates on both sides of that change.
    # ``tests/unit/test_route_table.py`` holds the floor.
    "fastapi>=0.115",
    # Direct floor for the Starlette ASGI layer so the resolved lockfile stays
    # above PYSEC-2026-161 even when pulled through FastAPI or MCP.
    "starlette>=1.0.1",
    "uvicorn>=0.30",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "rich>=13.0",
    "textual>=1.0",
    "click>=8.3.3",
    "openai>=2.36.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.13.1",
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.2",
    "setproctitle>=1.3",
    "prometheus-client>=0.21",
    "pluggy>=1.5",
    "mcp>=1.30.0,<2",
    "watchdog>=4.0",
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.41.1",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.41.1",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp>=1.41.1",
    "pillow>=12.3.0",
    "pyfiglet>=1.0",
    "terminaltexteffects>=0.11",
    "websockets>=14.0",
    # SAML XML signature verification. Pure-Python via lxml+cryptography.
    # Required to validate IdP assertions in src/bernstein/core/security/auth.py;
    # enabling SAML without this library installed is a hard error.
    "signxml>=4.0",
    # Hardened XML parser. Used in src/bernstein/core/security/auth.py to
    # parse SAML assertions without expanding internal entities. Mitigates
    # billion-laughs / quadratic-blowup DoS on unauthenticated IdP responses.
    # defusedxml.ElementTree is a drop-in for xml.etree.ElementTree.
    "defusedxml>=0.7.1",
    # OS-keychain transport for the credential vault (release 1.9). Pulls in
    # macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service / Windows Credential Manager
    # backends. AES-GCM file fallback uses the existing ``cryptography`` dep.
    "keyring>=25.0",
    # Strict per-phase artefact validation in
    # ``src/bernstein/core/orchestration/phase_schemas.py``.  Already pulled in
    # transitively by several deps; promoted to a direct dep so the phase
    # pipeline does not silently degrade if a transitive owner drops it.
    "jsonschema>=4.20",
    # RFC 3161 TimeStampToken ASN.1 parsing for the multi-tenant audit
    # export verifier. Pure-Python, MIT-licensed, ~250KB wheel; ships the
    # ``tsp.TSTInfo`` / ``cms.ContentInfo`` types we need without us
    # hand-rolling a DER parser. Used exclusively by
    # ``bernstein.core.security.rfc3161_verifier``.
    "asn1crypto>=1.5",
    # Canonical CBOR encoding for the COSE_Sign1 (RFC 9052) audit receipt.
    # MIT-licensed; deterministic-encoding mode gives byte-identical receipt
    # replay. Used by ``bernstein.core.security.audit_receipt`` and the
    # standalone ``tools/verify_audit_receipt.py`` verifier.
    "cbor2>=5.6",
    # Pure-Python PDF generation for the EU AI Act Article 12 evidence pack
    # rendered by `bernstein compliance pack`. MIT-licensed, no native deps.
    # Used exclusively by ``bernstein.core.compliance.article12``.
    "reportlab>=5,<6",
    # YAML frontmatter parsing for `bernstein ticket validate` (SDD ticket
    # schema). Lightweight, MIT-licensed; piggybacks on the already-pinned
    # PyYAML for the YAML body. The validator gracefully falls back to a
    # PyYAML-only parser so the dep is not strictly required at runtime,
    # but pinning it here keeps downstream behaviour consistent.
    "python-frontmatter>=1.1",
    # Pulled in transitively by httpx / anyio. Pin directly to >=3.15 so we
    # stay above the CVE-2026-45409 floor regardless of which transitive
    # owner resolves first; pip-audit gates the production closure on this.
    "idna>=3.15",
    # PEP 440 version parsing/comparison. Imported directly at runtime by the
    # ``bernstein doctor`` last-green advisory (``cli/commands/doctor_cmd.py``)
    # and the adapter security-floor / advisory gates
    # (``adapters/security_floor.py``, ``adapters/advisories.py``). Only ever
    # pulled into the lockfile transitively by dev/test tooling (pytest,
    # pip-audit, e2b, ...), so a clean ``uv tool install`` shipped without it
    # and ``bernstein doctor`` crashed with ModuleNotFoundError. Promoted to a
    # direct dependency so the resolver always installs it. Pure-Python.
    "packaging>=24",
    "tzdata>=2024.1",
]
