[project]
name = "punt-quarry"
version = "3.4.0"
description = "Extract searchable knowledge from any document. Expose it to LLMs via MCP."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
license = "MIT"
authors = [
    { name = "Punt Labs" },
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Text Processing :: Indexing",
]
dependencies = [
    "pymupdf>=1.25.0",
    # 0.34.0 is the first release carrying create_index(column, config=...);
    # every earlier version raises TypeError on the call db/schema.py and
    # db/optimizer.py make, so a resolver landing below this floor produces an
    # artifact that imports cleanly and fails at the first index build.
    "lancedb>=0.34.0",
    "tokenizers>=0.20.0",
    "huggingface-hub>=0.26.0",
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.0.0",
    # 0.133.0 is the first fastapi that drops its own starlette ceiling
    # (starlette>=0.40.0, unbounded); every earlier release caps starlette below
    # 1.3.1 and so cannot coexist with the secure floor below.
    "fastapi>=0.133.0,<1.0.0",
    "typer>=0.15.0",
    "rich>=13.0.0",
    # Floor is 2.x: the stdio server imports MCPServer from mcp.server.mcpserver,
    # which exists only in mcp 2.x (FastMCP was removed in 2.0). A 1.x install
    # satisfies the range and then fails at import, so the floor must exclude it.
    "mcp>=2.2.0,<3.0.0",
    # 1.3.1 is the first release patched against all five advisories open here:
    # the request.form() DoS and StaticFiles UNC SSRF (high), the Host-header and
    # HTTPEndpoint getattr issues (medium), and request.url.hostname poisoning.
    # No ceiling: the previous <1.0.0 is what made these unfixable by a version
    # bump at all, and fastapi -- which owns far more starlette surface than we
    # do -- carries none. uv.lock is the reproducibility mechanism.
    "starlette>=1.3.1",
    "uvicorn>=0.32.0",
    "websockets>=13.0",
    "pyarrow>=18.0.0",
    "numpy>=1.26.0",
    "Pillow>=10.0.0",
    "python-docx>=1.1.0",
    "tree-sitter>=0.23.0",
    "tree-sitter-language-pack>=0.5.0,<1.0.0",
    "rapidocr>=3.6.0",
    "onnxruntime>=1.18.0",
    "opencv-python-headless>=4.8.0",
    "openpyxl>=3.1.0",
    "python-pptx>=1.0.0",
    "beautifulsoup4>=4.12.0",
    "markdownify>=0.14.0",
    "pathspec>=0.12.0",
    "ultimate-sitemap-parser>=1.8.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.0",
    "cryptography>=46.0.0",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
    # Floor and cap both verified (Copilot, PR #503 round 3): this repo
    # subclasses watchdog's PRIVATE internals (Inotify._add_dir_watch/
    # _add_watch, InotifyBuffer.__init__, InotifyEmitter.on_thread_start --
    # see quarry/daemon/inotify_prune.py, inotify_prune_chain.py), and that
    # subclassed surface was verified only against the installed 6.0.0 (the
    # CI pin test, test_pins_the_watchdog_internals_this_module_subclasses,
    # never ran against an older release). The floor was previously >=4.0,
    # which was ALSO wrong independent of a naming issue Copilot separately
    # caught: fs_watchdog.py imports UnsupportedLibcError unconditionally,
    # but that class is named UnsupportedLibc (no "Error" suffix) through
    # watchdog 4.0.2, the last 4.x release -- confirmed by downloading and
    # inspecting watchdog/utils/__init__.py at 4.0.2 ("class
    # UnsupportedLibc(Exception)") versus 5.0.0 ("class
    # UnsupportedLibcError(Exception)"), so 4.x/5.x resolving under the old
    # floor would have crashed at import time. 6.0.0 is both the version
    # with the correct name AND the only version this module's private
    # internals dependency is verified against, so the floor and the cap
    # meet at the single release actually tested: 6.0.0 is currently
    # watchdog's latest release, so this pin resolves to exactly what CI
    # runs. A future watchdog release bumping either bound is a deliberate,
    # re-verified dependency update, not an automatic one.
    "watchdog>=6.0,<7",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    # 0.15.8 is the first ruff whose S603 stops flagging a subprocess call
    # with fully literal argv (bisected: 0.15.7 flags hooks.py:139, 0.15.8
    # does not).  Below it the repo cannot be green on any single source
    # state: the older ruff demands a `# noqa: S603` there and the newer
    # one rejects that same directive as unused (RUF100).
    "ruff>=0.15.8",
    "mypy>=1.18.1",
    "pyright>=1.1.0",
    "pytest>=8.4.2",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23.0",
    "pytest-cov>=6.0.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.3.0",
    "types-PyYAML>=6.0.0",
    # Enforces the DES-031 I1 client/engine package boundary (make check-imports).
    "import-linter>=2.0",
]
# Eval-only. NEVER a core dependency, NEVER a dependency of `make check` or any
# CI job. ranx pulls Numba/llvmlite (a C-JIT stack, not pure Python); it must
# stay quarantined here so a compiler-less install of quarry proper is never
# blocked. `make eval` runs `uv sync --extra eval`; nothing else needs it.
# Verified 2026-07-04: resolves + installs + imports on CPython 3.13.5 with
# numba 0.66.0 / llvmlite 0.48.0 wheels (no compiler required).
#
# numpy skew: ranx -> numba caps the resolved numpy to <2.5, so `uv.lock` (and
# thus CI, which installs the locked env) tests against numpy 2.4.6, while the
# shipped wheel and `make test-wheel` resolve numpy 2.5.x unconstrained. This is
# safe — the numpy 2.x C-ABI is stable across 2.4/2.5, so embeddings and search
# behave identically; only the eval harness pins the older numpy.
eval = [
    "ranx>=0.3.20",
]

quarry = "quarry.__main__:app"
quarryd = "quarry.daemon.launcher:entrypoint"
quarry-hook = "quarry._hook_entry:main"

    "A",    # flake8-builtins

    "PIE",  # flake8-pie
    "RSE",  # flake8-raise

    "TC003",  # Move standard lib import into TYPE_CHECKING

"src/quarry/cli_ingest.py" = ["FBT"]  # typer boolean CLI flags
"src/quarry/cli_sync.py" = ["FBT"]  # typer boolean CLI flags
"src/quarry/cli_project.py" = ["FBT"]  # typer boolean CLI flags
"src/quarry/cli_maintenance.py" = ["FBT"]  # typer boolean CLI flags
"src/quarry/cli_remote.py" = ["FBT"]  # typer boolean CLI flags
"src/quarry/daemon/launcher.py" = ["FBT"]  # typer boolean CLI flags

# Tests import _private internals (legitimate), use pytest fixture discovery
# (functions appear unused), and have fixture params without annotations.
[[tool.pyright.executionEnvironments]]
root = "tests"
reportPrivateUsage = false
reportUnusedFunction = false
reportMissingParameterType = false

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "8.0"
addopts = "-ra -q -m 'not slow and not embedding and not hook_integration'"
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
timeout = 30
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (run with -m slow)",
    "resource: long-lived-process resource-invariant tests (fd/memory leak guards)",
    "integration: real-socket/live-server tests, also slow so excluded from the fast CI suite and run via -m integration",
    "embedding: opts back in to the real ONNX model (410 MB); deselected by default alongside slow, run via -m embedding",
    "network: opts back in to real DNS resolution; the default suite resolves from a fake so it does not depend on the network",
    "hook_integration: spawns a real quarry-hook and/or quarryd subprocess; deselected by default, run via -m hook_integration",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src"]
omit = ["tests/*", "*/test_*.py"]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "def __str__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
]
show_missing = true
precision = 2

license = { text = "MIT" }

classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",

    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Atmospheric Science",
]
# Depends ONLY on the substrate (legoesm-core) — NOT on the other Earth-system
# components, NOR on the coupler/driver/training above it.  Both invariants are
# machine-enforced by the import-linter contracts ("Earth-system components are
# independent of each other" + "Components must not import the coupler, driver,
# or training"), which is what lets `pip install legoesm-atmosphere` run standalone.
dependencies = [

    "numpy>=1.26",
    "equinox>=0.11",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
]

# Optional heavy feature reaching UP into the ML layer.  The BASE atmosphere
# imports only legoesm-core (verified: `import legoesm.atmosphere` does not pull
# ml), so the component stays standalone; this extra declares the install path
# for the SFNO/U-Cast neural dynamical cores + ML physics parameterization, which
# import the neural primitives at top level:
#   atmosphere.dynamics.{sfno_sw,sfno_pe,ucast_pe} and
#   atmosphere.physics.ml_parameterization
#   -> legoesm.ml.{sfno,ucast,normalization,channel_packing,conservation,physics.*}

description = "Single-agent task runner for hardened Podman containers"

license = "Apache-2.0"
authors = [
    {name = "Jiri Vyskocil", email = "jiri@vyskocil.com"},
]

]

    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Environment :: Console",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: System Administrators",
    "Operating System :: POSIX :: Linux",
    "Programming Language :: Python",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",

    "Topic :: Software Development :: Quality Assurance",

requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.15"

]

Homepage = "https://terok-ai.github.io/terok-executor/"

Issues = "https://github.com/terok-ai/terok-executor/issues"

[project.scripts]
terok-executor = "terok_executor.cli:main"

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["terok_executor"]
combine-as-imports = true

[tool.ruff.format]

docstring-code-format = true

# Static type checking -- see `make typecheck`.
# ``resources/`` is excluded entirely: it holds container-side scripts and
# bundled agent assets that aren't part of the host-side import graph
# (``resources/toad-agents/`` isn't even a valid Python package name).
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
files = ["src/terok_executor"]
exclude = "src/terok_executor/resources/"
ignore_missing_imports = true
check_untyped_defs = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unreachable = true
no_implicit_optional = true
strict_equality = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
pretty = true
show_error_codes = true

# ``resources/`` holds container-side scripts (run inside task containers, not
# part of the host import graph -- the same reason mypy excludes it).  Tests
# exercise them by path-loading (``SourceFileLoader``), which coverage.py can't
# attribute, so they report 0%; omit them rather than chase phantom misses.
[tool.coverage.run]
omit = ["*/terok_executor/resources/*"]
